sentences.text: This petition has been filed by all the accused challenging initiation of criminal proceedings against them for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. The respondent No.2 had lodged a complaint on 26.01.2018 contending that she had married the accused No.1 on 03.11.2014 and at the time of marriage, certain dowry was given.
She thereafter alleged that about a month after the marriage she was harassed continuously by her husband, by her in-laws and also by her sister-in-law and brother-in-law.
She stated in the complaint that she was unable to bear the harassment she had gone back to her parent's home and her husband had come over to her parent's home on 28.12.2017 and had assaulted her.
She therefore, sought for initiation of NC: 2024:KHC:19775 proceedings against her husband and her in-laws for the continuous dowry harassment meted out by her.
3. Pursuant to the investigation conducted by the police, a charge sheet was also laid against the petitioners.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the averments made in the complaint would indicate that complaint was lodged nearly a year after the alleged incident and this itself would indicate that this was a false complaint.

He also submitted that prior to lodging of the complaint, the complainant had initiated proceedings under Section 125 of Cr.P.C seeking maintenance and in those proceedings accused No.1 i.e., husband and the complainant had entered into an agreement whereby the husband/accused No.1 had agreed to convey 15 guntas of land and these documents would clearly indicate that the complainant was initiating criminal proceedings to harass the accused.
5.
A reading of the complaint and also the statements produced would indicate that the allegations made against NC: 2024:KHC:19775 the in-laws, sister-in-law and brother-in-law are general in nature.
There are no specific allegations made of any ill- treatment to the complainant by accused No.1/husband from the year 2014 till the date of filing of complaint.
In fact, the only allegation narrated in the complaint is the assault by the husband in the year 2017 at the complainant's paternal home.
In fact, the complainant admits in the complaint that she was residing in her paternal home and this itself would indicate that the probability of any harassment by the in-laws does not arise.
It is therefore clear that the proceedings initiated as against the in-laws, sister-in-law and brother-in-law i.e., accused Nos.2 to 5 cannot be sustained.
6. However, the complaint does indicate an incident of assault by the husband and therefore the proceedings against him would therefore necessarily have to continue.
It is open for accused No.1/husband to put forth his defence regarding the settlement arrived at with his wife to establish that there was no dowry harassment.
Subject to above, the proceedings initiated as against petitioner Nos.2 to 5 shall stand quashed.
